question:
A 59-year-old female presents to the ED with symptoms of recurring chest pressure accompanied by
jaw pain radiation. Her ECG demonstrates ST-segment elevation, while cardiac enzyme levels remain
normal on both initial and follow-up testing hours later. Her vital signs show a heart rate of 82/min and
blood pressure of 124/73 mm Hg. Upon cardiac examination, heart sounds are regular without any
friction rub detected. Given this patient's suspected diagnosis, which therapeutic combination would be
most appropriate? Answer Choices: (A) Aspirin, clopidogrel, beta blockers, and nitrates (B) Aspirin and
beta blockers (C) Aspirin and clopidogrel (D) Beta blockers, nitrates, and aspirin (E) Statins and beta
blockers (F) Calcium channel blockers and nitrates (G) Low molecular weight heparin and nitrates (H)
ACE inhibitors and aspirin (I) Nitrates only (J) Coronary stenting with dual antiplatelet therapy
 A. Nitrates only
B. Aspirin, clopidogrel, beta blockers, and nitrates
C. Coronary stenting with dual antiplatelet therapy
D. ACE inhibitors and aspirin
E. Beta blockers, nitrates, and aspirin
F. Statins and beta blockers
G. Low molecular weight heparin and nitrates
H. Aspirin and beta blockers
I. Calcium channel blockers and nitrates

J. Aspirin and clopidogrel
